look_here_first: Recognize the woody evergreen-ish shrub first: many short branches carry small aromatic oval/elliptic leaves and comparatively large showy flowers that can vary from red and pink to white.
project_tracker_diagnostic: woody perennial subshrub/shrub; small aromatic elliptic to obovate leaves; often evergreen or tardily deciduous; showy relatively large flowers with strong color variation; dry rocky western Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos habitat

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bandera — NPSOT states the wild Texas range begins in western Bandera County and extends westward. Edwards — a documented NPSOT photo-contest field record places wild Salvia greggii at Kickapoo Caverns State Park, Edwards County. Kew confirms Texas as native, but a third explicit project-target county native occurrence has not yet been documented to the project standard.

approval_exception.reason: User explicitly approved canonical inclusion despite only two independently documented target-zone counties. Evidence status remains UNRESOLVED; no third county was invented.

best_field_traits: small aromatic elliptic to obovate leaves
showy relatively large flowers with strong color variation
dry rocky western Edwards Plateau/Trans-Pecos habitat

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia ballotiflora: S. greggii has larger showier flowers and generally larger less-hairy leaves; S. ballotiflora has tiny blue-purple flowers and small hairy rough leaves.
